article_title: Stress, stressors and related factors in clinical learning of midwifery students in Iran: a cross sectional study.
citation: Rezaei Behrooz, Falahati Juliana, Beheshtizadeh Raziyeh. (2020). Stress, stressors and related factors in clinical learning of midwifery students in Iran: a cross sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1970-7
title: Persian Questionnaire of Stressful Sources (PQSS) for clinical learning stressors
description: The PQSS is a 29-item, four-point Likert questionnaire developed by Iranian researchers that "evaluates the sources of stress in clinical learning environment from nursing and midwifery students’ view point". It measures four dimensions: interpersonal communication (8 items), clinical practices (8 items), unpleasant emotions (7 items) and humiliating experiences (6 items), with total scores ranging from 29 to 116. In this study its reliability was confirmed with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.94, and it was administered alongside the Persian 14-item Cohen Perceived Stress Scale.
requirements: Respondents must have clinical learning experience; the study included only students who had passed at least one semester of internship
constraints: Test-retest reliability and content validity confirmed only in national (Iranian) studies; scores depend on self-report
target_learning_goals: identifying sources of stress in clinical learning environments
examples: Used in the 2016 cross-sectional survey of 70 Iranian midwifery students, yielding a total mean score of 2.14 ± 0.50 on a 1–4 scale
key_sources: Rezaei Behrooz, Falahati Juliana, Beheshtizadeh Raziyeh. (2020). Stress, stressors and related factors in clinical learning of midwifery students in Iran: a cross sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1970-7

article_title: Using psychometric tools as a window into students' quantitative reasoning in introductory physics
citation: Trevor I. Smith, Philip Eaton, Suzanne White Brahmia, Alexis Olsho, Andrew Boudreaux, Chris DePalma, Victor LaSasso, Christopher Whitener, Scott Straguzzi. (2019). Using psychometric tools as a window into students' quantitative reasoning in introductory physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05491
title: Physics quantitative literacy as a conceptual blend of physics concepts and mathematical reasoning with three reasoning subdomains
description: The article frames physics quantitative literacy (PQL) as "a conceptual blend between physics concepts and mathematical reasoning," drawing on conceptual blending theory. PQL is operationalized through three principle reasoning subdomains previously identified in mathematics and physics education research: ratios and proportions, covariation, and signed (negative) quantities. The psychometric results qualify this framework: the article suggests that either students' PQL cannot be separated into these three skills, or their skills in these areas have developed similarly such that they are functionally equivalent.
requirements: Assessment items must isolate types of mathematical reasoning that are independent of each other in physics questions, which the article names as the PIQL's design challenge
constraints: Student response data do not reproduce the expert three-construct grouping; the framework's separability at the student level is an open question the article poses explicitly
examples: The PIQL's twenty questions are grouped by the designers to probe the three subdomains, and module analysis reveals connections between the constructs in student reasoning
key_sources: Trevor I. Smith, Philip Eaton, Suzanne White Brahmia, Alexis Olsho, Andrew Boudreaux, Chris DePalma, Victor LaSasso, Christopher Whitener, Scott Straguzzi. (2019). Using psychometric tools as a window into students' quantitative reasoning in introductory physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05491

article_title: The Physics Inventory of Quantitative Literacy: A tool for assessing mathematical reasoning in introductory physics
citation: White Brahmia, S. W., Olsho, A., Smith, T. I., Boudreaux, A., Eaton, P., and Zimmerman, C. (2020). The Physics Inventory of Quantitative Literacy: A tool for assessing mathematical reasoning in introductory physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10865
title: Physics quantitative literacy as proceptual reasoning: a conceptual blend of mathematics and physical meaning-making
description: The article grounds the PIQL in the framework of conceptual blending theory and proceptual understanding. Gray and Tall "define proceptual understanding as a combination of procedural mastery and con ceptual understanding", and the article treats reasoning about physics quantities as an inseparable blend of mathematical procedure and physical meaning, interpreted through Fauconnier and Turner's conceptual blending theory and Sherin's symbolic forms. Expert mathematization develops through creation of new blended cognitive spaces rather than addition of physics quantities to existing algebraic structures. The PIQL's three facets are designed to probe this blended reasoning.
requirements: Items must require blending of mathematical procedure with physical context rather than computation alone
constraints: Symbolic forms are treated as a learning objective for typical introductory students, not as a description of how they currently think
target_learners: students in calculus-based introductory physics courses
target_learning_goals: developing proceptual, blended quantitative reasoning about physical quantities
examples: The PIQL item in Fig. 3 relies on the quantity and scaling symbolic forms, exemplifying proceptual understanding of the negative sign in a mathematics-physics blend
key_sources: White Brahmia, S. W., Olsho, A., Smith, T. I., Boudreaux, A., Eaton, P., and Zimmerman, C. (2020). The Physics Inventory of Quantitative Literacy: A tool for assessing mathematical reasoning in introductory physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10865

article_title: Assessing physics quantitative literacy development in algebra-based physics
citation: Charlotte Zimmerman, Alexis Olsho, Trevor I. Smith, Philip Eaton, and Suzanne White Brahmia. (2025). Assessing physics quantitative literacy development in algebra-based physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14771
title: Three-facet framework of physics quantitative literacy (PQL)
description: Physics quantitative literacy (PQL) is defined as quantitative literacy situated in physics contexts, a conceptual blend between physics and mathematical reasoning. The framework, inherited from the PIQL, holds that the PIQL "was designed to measure three main facets of PQL: reasoning about signs, covariational reasoning, and proportional reasoning". In this framework proportional reasoning is the linear subset of covariational reasoning: "proportional reasoning describes covariational reasoning about quantities related by a linear function".
requirements: Assessment items must be interpreted against the three facets of sign reasoning, covariational reasoning, and proportional reasoning
constraints: In algebra-based courses, covariation is restricted to linear rates of change, single-variable contexts, and scalars rather than vectors
target_learners: students in introductory physics courses, algebra-based or calculus-based
target_learning_goals: interpreting signs of physical quantities, covariational reasoning, and proportional reasoning in physics contexts
examples: The GERQN Bottle item asks students to select the graph relating water height to water volume in a cylindrical bottle, probing covariational reasoning without calculus
key_sources: Charlotte Zimmerman, Alexis Olsho, Trevor I. Smith, Philip Eaton, and Suzanne White Brahmia. (2025). Assessing physics quantitative literacy development in algebra-based physics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14771
